sourceInventory.meaning: Section 97 concerns relativity of distance. A rigid rod is at rest in K_1; K_1 moves at speed v relative to K. Its rest-frame/proper length is l_0.
Figure 223 belongs to the rod/frame setup; retain its identity and textual reference without examining the image.
Length l in K is the separation of the moving rod's endpoint positions recorded simultaneously according to clocks of K, not a photographic appearance or measurements at arbitrary different times.

For the longitudinal rod, l=l_0 sqrt(1-v^2/c^2), labeled (8.2). The factor is less than one for nonzero subluminal motion, so the same rod is shorter in the moving-frame measurement. At v=0 the lengths are equal.

The relativity of endpoint distance follows jointly from invariant light speed in inertial frames and time dilation. Reuse the preceding optical-clock idea, now with the rod parallel rather than perpendicular to relative motion. Do not extend longitudinal contraction to transverse dimensions.
A pulse leaves end A, reflects at the mirror on end B, and returns to A. A clock at rest with the rod in K_1 measures the full round-trip proper interval tau_0. Figure 224 belongs here.

K's clocks measure tau between the same emission and return events. These events occur at the same rod endpoint in K_1 but at different positions in K. Equation (8.1) connects tau and tau_0 by time dilation.
tau_1 and tau_2 are respectively outbound A-to-B and return B-to-A durations in K, and their sum is the full interval tau.
Figure 225 tracks simultaneous rod configurations AB at emission, A_1B_1 after tau_1, and A_2B_2 after tau_1+tau_2. During the outbound interval the rod translates by v tau_1.
In K the outbound mirror recedes. The pulse travels l+v tau_1 at speed c, yielding tau_1=l/(c-v).

On return, A advances toward the pulse by v tau_2; the return-route distance is l-v tau_2, not l=v tau_2. The adjacent source balance already has the physically correct minus sign. The registered p0261-math-1 correction must change only the erroneous modern token, preserving the faithful source.
Summing the two K-frame intervals gives equation (8.4), not the proper-frame round-trip value.
Equations (8.1) and (8.3) also give the same tau as equation (8.5).
Equating (8.4) with (8.5) implies l/l_0=sqrt(1-v^2/c^2), recovering (8.2); do not infer length expansion or introduce a second incompatible clock interval.
Measured endpoint distance is not an absolute frame-independent quantity; its longitudinal value depends on the object's relative speed.

For the same rod, rest-frame length is largest. Reversing the setup so the rod rests in K gives l_0 in K and the contracted length in K_1. This follows from the relativity principle: no preferred inertial frame; contraction is reciprocal.

The historical Eddington/Gulliver passage expresses the counterintuitive reciprocity of contraction. Preserve that physical point through actual frame-dependent simultaneous measurements, without teaching a fictional size/appearance paradox.
No source questions, numbered exercises, solutions, choices, or answers belong to this card.

assumptions: K and K_1 are inertial; choose positive x along the rod's motion and A-to-B direction in the stated optical-clock setup.
0<=v<c; l and l_0 are positive. Strict contraction requires 0<v<c.
In K, the simultaneous endpoint separation is l and A(t)=vt, B(t)=l+vt.
The light pulse has speed c in each inertial frame; reflection is at moving endpoint B.
independentPhysicsDerivation.outbound: From A(0)=0, x_light(t)=ct. Reflection satisfies c tau_1=l+v tau_1, so tau_1=l/(c-v).
independentPhysicsDerivation.return: At reflection B_1=l+v tau_1. At reception A_2=v(tau_1+tau_2). The positive return distance B_1-A_2=l-v tau_2=c tau_2, so tau_2=l/(c+v). The pulse displacement is negative, but its traveled distance and tau_2 are positive.
independentPhysicsDerivation.properClock: Emission and return occur at A in K_1, hence tau_0=2l_0/c and tau=gamma tau_0=(2l_0/c) gamma.
independentPhysicsDerivation.contraction: Equating the two expressions for the same tau gives l gamma^2=l_0 gamma, hence l=l_0/gamma=l_0 sqrt(1-v^2/c^2).
independentPhysicsDerivation.transverse: The derived contraction concerns the component parallel to relative motion. The preceding perpendicular optical clock motivates time dilation, not contraction of transverse dimensions.
independentPhysicsDerivation.symmetry: Each inertial observer measures the length of a rod moving relative to that observer using simultaneous endpoints in that observer's own frame. The measurements use different simultaneity slices, so reciprocal contraction is not a contradiction or an optical illusion.
